```{r}
# Beginning with head and tail of data to see the top 6 and bottom 6 rows of
# the data frame

clean_data <- read.csv("Cleaned_Commute.csv")

head(clean_data)
tail(clean_data)
```

```{r}
# Random slice of 6 rows from data frame to get a sense of the variation in the 
# data frame. Seed used to ensure reproducibility

set.seed(723)

clean_data |>
slice_sample(n = 6)
```

```{r}
# Running glimpse to check the variable class of each column of data frame

clean_data |>
  glimpse()
```

```{r}
# Creating a summary table that is grouped by Mode & Gender to create summary 
# statistics that are meaningful, rather than mixing four different modes of 
# transportation (which would not create meaningful or comparable statistics)

clean_data |>
  group_by(Mode, Gender) |>
  summarise( 
    n = n(),
    national_pct = sum(Count) / sum(Total) * 100, 
    min_pct = min(Percent),
    median_pct = median(Percent), 
    mean_pct = mean(Percent), 
    max_pct = max(Percent), 
    .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
  rename(
    "Mode" = Mode, 
    "Gender" = Gender, 
    "National (%)" = national_pct, 
    "Mean (%)" = mean_pct,
    "Median (%)" = median_pct, 
    "Minimum (%)" = min_pct, 
    "Maximum (%)" = max_pct
  ) |> 
  tt() |> 
  format_tt(j = 3:8, digits = 1, num_fmt = "decimal") |>
  style_tt(j = 1:8, align = "llrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
# Testing that categories (Mode, Gender, and Geography) align with expected n

mode_counts   <- count(commute_clean, Mode)
gender_counts <- count(commute_clean, Gender)
geography_counts <- count(commute_clean, Geography)

stopifnot(
  "Expected exactly 4 modes" = nrow(mode_counts) == 4,
  "Each mode should have 26 rows (13 provinces x 2 genders)" = 
    all(mode_counts$n == 26),
  "Modes are not the expected four" = setequal(
    mode_counts$Mode,
    c("Car, truck or van", "Public transit", "Active transportation", 
      "Other method")
  ),
  "Expected exactly 2 genders" = nrow(gender_counts) == 2,
  "Each gender should have 52 rows (13 provinces x 4 modes)" = 
    all(gender_counts$n == 52),
  "Gender values are not Men+ and Women+" = 
    setequal(gender_counts$Gender, c("Men+", "Women+")),
  "Expected exactly 13 provinces and territories" = 
    n_distinct(commute_clean$Geography) == 13
)
```

```{r}
# Transit share by province, men vs. women
# Writing in test to ensure that there are 26 rows

transit_eda <- commute_clean |> 
  filter(Mode == "Public transit")

nrow(transit_eda) # should be 26
stopifnot(nrow(transit_eda) == 26)
```
```{r}
# Plotting transit use percentage points by Geography & Gender to visualize
# potential gendered and/or geographic differences in transit use.

ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Percent, y = fct_reorder(Geography, Percent), 
                        colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) +
  labs(
    title = "What Does the Distribution of Transit Users Look Like Across 
    Canadian Provinces and Territories?", 
    x = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```

```{r}
# Visualizing gender difference in transit use (Women+ minus Men+) by province 
# to visualize which provinces/territories have the largest & smallest gender 
# differences in transit use (as well as if there are provinces/territories 
# with inverted gender differences)

gap <- gap |>
  mutate(direction = if_else(gap_pp > 0, "Women+ higher", "Men+ higher"))

ggplot(gap, aes(x = gap_pp, y = fct_reorder(Geography, gap_pp), fill = direction)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Women+ higher" = "#6CCED9", "Men+ higher" = "#EC9C3E")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "What Does the Distribution of Transit Users Look Like Across 
    Canadian Provinces and Territories?", 
    x = "Gap in percentage points (Women+ minus Men+)",
    y = "Canadian Provinces & Territories",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
```{r}
gap <- transit_eda |>
  select(Geography, Gender, Percent) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = Gender, values_from = Percent) |>
  mutate(
    gap_pp = `Women+` - `Men+`,        # difference in percentage points
    ratio  = `Women+` / `Men+`         # how many times higher women's share is
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(gap_pp)) 

gap |>
  tt() |>
   format_tt(j = 4, digits = 1, num_fmt = "decimal") |>
  setNames(c("Province", "Men+", "Women+", "Gap (pp)", "Ratio"))
```

```{r}
# Creating a list of province/territory abbreviations for following graph's 
# labels (to reduce clutter on graph)

prov_abbr <- c(
  "Newfoundland and Labrador" = "NL", 
  "Prince Edward Island" = "PEI", 
  "Nova Scotia" = "NS", 
  "New Brunswick" = "NB", 
  "Quebec" = "QC", 
  "Ontario" = "ON", 
  "Manitoba" = "MB", 
  "Saskatchewan" = "SK", 
  "Alberta" = "AB", 
  "British Columbia" = "BC", 
  "Yukon" = "YT", 
  "Northwest Territories" = "NWT", 
  "Nunavut" = "NU"
)
```

```{r}
# Plotting each province/territory by transit use percentage and total number of
# commuters (plotting each province/territory twice - one for each gender)
# Logarithmic scale used to account for significant differences between 
# commuter totals in small provinces/territories (such as NU, NWT, and YT) and 
# commuter totals in large provinces (such as ON, BC, and QC)

ggplot(transit_eda, aes(x = Total, y = Percent, colour = Gender)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) prov_abbr[x]) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = unname(prov_abbr[Geography])),
                size = 3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_comma()) + 
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 12),
    breaks = seq(0, 12, by = 2),
    labels = \(x) paste0(x)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Women+" = "#6CCED9", "Men+" = "#EC9C3E")) + 
  labs(
    title = "Does a Province/Territory Size Relate to its Share of Commuters?", 
    x = "Total commuters (log scale)", 
    y = "Commuters using public transit (%)", 
    colour = "Gender"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold")) 
```
# Reflections on EDA
I am not surprised to see that there are large variations in commuter and 
transit totals between provinces/territories due to population numbers and 
robustness of transit systems between large provinces (such as ON, BC, and QC) 
and small or rural provinces/territories (such as NU, NWT, YT).

Additionally, women use transit more than men in the majority of the 13 
provinces/territories (10 of 13). While the difference between men's and women's 
transit use is only between 0.2-4.6 percentage points (pp), it does point to a trend 
that I would follow and examine further if I were doing statistical analysis on
this dataset/research question.

What did surprise me is that there are 3 provinces/territories that had an 
inverse relationship between gender and transit use (NWT, NU, and NL). Upon 
first seeing this, I wondered if this could have something to do with northern 
climate/environment and masculinity, but upon thinking through this further, I 
don't know if this theory would hold considering that Yukon has a positive 
gender gap of 0.7 pp in comparison to Newfoundland & Labrador's (NL) -0.8 pp 
gap.
